title: Why Metal Feels Colder than Wood
subject: Physics
objective: A steel railing and a wooden bench at the same 10 °C, yet the steel feels icy. Skin senses how fast heat leaves it, and metal conducts heat hundreds of times faster than wood.

fill.q: A material that conducts heat well is called a ____.
A material that conducts heat poorly is called an ____.
Objects kept in the same room reach the same ____.
Our skin senses the rate of ____ flow, not temperature directly.
The property that measures how fast a material conducts heat is thermal ____.

tf.q: A steel railing at 10 °C is colder than a wooden bench at 10 °C.
tf.explain: Both are at the same temperature; steel only feels colder.

tf.q: Wood is a poor conductor of heat.
tf.explain: Its thermal conductivity is about 0.1–0.2 W/m·K.

tf.q: On a hot day, metal feels hotter than wood at the same temperature.
tf.explain: Metal conducts heat into the skin faster.

tf.q: Copper conducts heat better than glass.

ar.a: Metal feels colder than wood at the same temperature.
ar.r: Metal conducts heat away from the skin much faster.

ar.a: A wooden spoon stays cool in hot soup.
ar.r: Wood is a poor conductor of heat.

short.q: Explain why a metal railing feels colder than a wooden bench on a winter morning.
short.solution: Both are at the air temperature. Skin senses heat loss: metal conducts heat away from the finger quickly so the skin cools; wood conducts slowly and the touched spot warms, so little heat is lost.

short.q: Why does the same metal feel hotter than wood on a hot afternoon?
short.solution: Now the objects are hotter than skin; metal conducts heat into the skin much faster than wood, so it feels hotter.
